GDS may delete any material it considers likely to do so or be affected by such activity and exercise powers under clause 12.

6.4 The DVS may retain Synthetic Data and test outputs for legitimate testing purposes, subject to confidentiality, security, intellectual property and non-misrepresentation obligations.

6.5 GDS may reset, replace or delete Synthetic Data and Sandbox configurations at any time. It will provide reasonable notice via DVS Governance forums of such intention where practicable

7. Reporting and responsible disclosure

7.1 The DVS will comply without limitation with the reporting requirements as specified in the Acceptable Use Policies.

8. Confidentiality and public statements

8.1 Each party, whether GDS or the DVS (the “receiving party”) may receive confidential information belonging to the other (the “disclosing party”) which has been obtained from the disclosing party whether directly or indirectly in connection with Sandbox and/or these Terms.

8.2 The receiving party may only use Confidential Information for the purposes set out in Clause 2 and shall not:

8.2.1 disclose it outside its organisation without the disclosing party’s prior written permission, except to personnel, contractors, subcontractors, professional advisers or auditors who need to know it and are subject to equivalent confidentiality obligations;

8.2.2 disclose, use or exploit the disclosing party’s Confidential Information without the disclosing party’s prior written consent, except for the purposes anticipated under these Terms.

8.3 The DVS remains responsible for any person to whom it discloses GDS Confidential Information.

8.4 The recipient party will immediately notify the disclosing party if it suspects unauthorised access, copying, use or disclosure of the Confidential Information.

8.5 Notwithstanding the other provisions of this clause 8:

8.5.1 a party may disclose information where required by law, a competent authority, parliamentary accountability, audit and/or applicable public-sector disclosure obligations. Where lawful and practicable, it should notify the other party and limit disclosure to what is required.

8.5.2 A party may also disclose information where it has previously received it from a third party without obligation of confidentiality, where it was in the public domain at the time of the disclosure (without the party being in breach) or where the information was independently developed without access to the disclosing party’s Confidential Information.

8.6 GDS may require the DVS to correct or remove any inaccurate or misleading statement or unauthorised use of branding promptly.

9. Intellectual property and feedback

9.1 Each party retains ownership of its intellectual property which it owned immediately prior to the launch of Sandbox (“Background IPR”). The DVS retains ownership of the software, integration implementation, architecture, code and proprietary logic that it develops in connection with its use and access to Sandbox. GDS retains ownership, on behalf of the Crown where applicable, of each element of the Sandbox as it may be developed after its launch.

9.2 “Feedback” means comments, questions, suggestions, bug reports and recommendations about the Sandbox, Test App, APIs, documentation or GOV.UK Wallet integration capability. It does not include DVS source code, the DVS’s proprietary implementation, DVS’s Background IPR, Personal Data or other material expressly agreed between GDS and the DVS to be excluded from the definition of Feedback.

9.3 The DVS grants DSIT a non-exclusive, perpetual, irrevocable, worldwide, royalty-free, transferable and sublicensable licence to use, adapt and incorporate Feedback for service, product and documentation improvement and for internal governance purposes.

9.4 If there is an IPR Claim, the responsible party will indemnify the other against all losses, damages, costs or expenses (including professional fees and fines) incurred as a result.

9.5 If an IPR Claim is made or anticipated by a party they will as soon as practicable inform the other. If such IPR Claim:

relates to GDS breaching another entity’s IPR in the Sandbox, GDS will have the right to immediately require cessation of use of the Sandbox by the DVS and the DVS will promptly comply; or

relates to material that DVS has introduced in access or use of the Sandbox then it will immediately cease use of Sandbox until it can satisfy GDS acting reasonably that permitting DVS to restart access and/or use of the Sandbox will not cause any breach of third party IPR.

9.6 Each Party acknowledges and agrees that it shall act in a spirit of good faith, mutual co-operation and collaboration in progressing the implementation and effectiveness and efficiency of the Sandbox to achieve the Purpose and Scope set out in Clause 2. Pursuant to that objective, the Parties agree that they will use reasonable endeavours to agree marketing and promotion material regarding Sandbox and the activities being undertaken for their mutual benefit.

9.7 Without prejudice or limitation to any of the previous provisions DVS shall not:

9.7.1 use the name, logos, brand materials, trademarks or other marks related to HMG, GOV.UK or GOV.UK Wallet or their promotion without express written permission of GDS.

9.7.2 make any press announcements or publicise this arrangement or its contents in any way whether for promotion,marketing or otherwise without consent of GDS which shall not be unreasonably withheld;

Technical Documentation

The technical specifications, integration guides, API documentation, configuration information, test flow documentation, or other technical materials issued or updated by GDS to support use of the Sandbox. This will be available at docs.wallet.service.gov.uk

Test App

The simulation application of the Wallet distributed by GDS for use in the Sandbox. |

UK Digital Verification Services Trust Framework

The set of rules, standards, requirements, certification arrangements, which the Secretary of State is required to maintain and publish pursuant to Section 32 of the Data (Use and Access) Act and which is available at https://www.gov.uk/government/collections/uk-digital-verification-services-trust-framework

“UK DVS Register” or “Register”

The register maintained by the Secretary of State under the Data (Use and Access) Act 2025 of organisations that provide digital identity and attribute services and which are certified as meeting the rules of the UK Digital Verification Services Trust Framework.

“UK GDPR”

has the meaning as set out in Section 3(10) of the DPA 2018, supplemented by Section 205(4) of the DPA 2018;
